title: Wrong-typed archetype_id silently treated as absent (fail-open) instead of fail-fast
detail: A numeric/bool/null archetype_id yields "" and silently becomes "no archetype" (pure demand event) — the spec's fail-fast for unknown archetype_id is bypassed. jint_strict was hardened for this exact class; string fields have no strict accessor.
recommended_fix: Type-assert json.String explicitly: if the key exists but isn't a string, return a named load error — only a genuinely absent key means no archetype.

title: Step tick-latch is non-strict — tick == state.tick re-runs the tick despite the 'strictly monotonic' claim
detail: The guard rejects only backward ticks; a caller passing tick == state.tick proceeds through state.tick = tick and re-runs commands/flow/eval for the same tick without latching replay_error — the 'never silent' latch misses the equality case.
recommended_fix: Change to `if tick <= state.tick { state.replay_error = true; return }` — all callers step from state.tick + 1, so equality is never legitimate.

title: Era set-piece index truncated to u16 with no roster cap (archetypes got a 255 cap for the same reason)
detail: More than 65535 set-pieces in one era wraps u16(si): dedup keys collide (crisis_active_for matches the wrong activation) and banner rows mislabel. crises.json was capped at 255 for exactly this truncation class; set_pieces have no cap.
recommended_fix: Cap era set-piece count at load (<= 65535, or 255 for symmetry) with a named error, mirroring the archetype roster cap.
